items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: The interviewee, Johnny Wiggs, discusses Joe Oliver extensively but never mentions John Wigington Hyman in the provided transcript context. John Wigington Hyman is identified as the interviewee's own birth name in the metadata/introductory turn, not as a separate person he has a relationship with.

ctx.x: You mentioned once before that the three great musicians, Snoozer of course we were talking about, and Louie and Bix, you didn't mention Joe Oliver. At other times you've told me you thought Joe Oliver had something that Louie never quite got. We all know Louie, he's wonderful. I'm trying to knock in.

Yeah, I think, well of course Louie doesn't have much resemblance to Joe Oliver anymore, although I think he's, uh, contrary to most, uh, died in the world jazz people, I think he's a very great performer, jazz performer today. He just hasn't been in good settings. But Joe Oliver had a dirty tone, which Louie almost got to perfection when Louie first hit New York. Of course Louie, uh, breathed on, on everything that Joe Oliver did, you know? Yeah. I mean, he studied Joe Oliver as close as a person could ever…

One thing I plan to ask you, if there's anything you can tell us about Tom Brown, since we never got to talk to him, or any of our Tulane tapes. I know you played with him, recorded with him a lot. Any remarks about him?
